components.note: Definition (G-measurable, all-event integral identity with integrals defined), a.e. version convention, P(B|G), E(X|Y) and C_G notation stated; the boundary of the version notion (which null modifications remain versions, with the trivial-G witness) is stated and proved.

locators.content: definition of E(X|F): (i) F-measurable, (ii) equal integrals over A in F

components.note: Integrability via A={Z>0} (source Lemma 4.1.1), uniqueness via A_n={Z>=Z'+1/n}, existence by Radon-Nikodym on (Omega,G) for X^+ and X^- with infinite-value sets removed; all steps written; no completeness used.
Linearity, expectation identity, order, |C X|<=C|X|, known information (Ex 4.1.3), independence (Ex 4.1.4), locality on B in G (Thm 4.1.2) and 0<=P(A|G)<=1, each proved on conditioning events.

Nonnegative extended extension by truncation with uniqueness and order, conditional monotone convergence (source 4.1.9(c), generalized to infinite mean), conditional Fatou and dominated convergence with written proofs; the source's decreasing-sequence Remark is a separate proved theorem with a model showing E|Y_1|<infinity cannot be dropped, plus a worked two-cell example.

locators.content: Theorem 4.1.9(c) and Remark on Y_n decreasing with E|Y_1|,E|Y|<infinity

components.note: Conditional Jensen with E|X|,E|phi(X)|<infinity; the source's set S of rational (a,b) with ax+b<=phi is an exact supremum representation for nonaffine phi and is proved (two supporting lines of different slope, convex combination with rational slope, rational intercept); separate affine case and the irrational-slope reason proved; countable exceptional union taken as in the source's Remark.

locators.content: Theorem 4.1.10, S={(a,b) in Q^2: ax+b<=phi(x)}, Remark on countable exceptional sets
use of (4.1.4) in proof of Theorem 4.1.11

components.note: L^p(G) as a.e. classes for 1<=p<infinity, ||X||_p, ||X||_infinity, L^infinity(G), the same notation for F_0, and the L^2 inner product are defined.

Norm axioms for finite p (Minkowski via convexity of |t|^p and Holder) and p=infinity (infimum attained a.e.) proved; contraction for 1<=p<infinity by conditional Jensen and E(C_G Y)=EY (source proof of 4.1.11), for p=infinity by conditioning the essential bound; difference inequality and preservation of convergence.
Both tower identities (source 4.1.13 (i),(ii)) and the measurable-version reduction (source 4.1.12) proved; necessity of nesting witnessed by the three-point noncommuting example.

Source four-step procedure (indicator, simple, monotone limit, positive/negative parts) written in full, including the nonnegative extended version with 0*infinity convention and integrability of Z C_G X without E|Z|<infinity.

Finite or countable partitions with cellwise averages (source Example 4.1.5), extended to null cells with free finite values, trivial sigma-algebra case and recovery of the finite formula; measurability of unions of cells and absolute convergence proved.

Factorization of real and nonnegative extended sigma(Y)-measurable Z through simple lifts with disjointified preimages and limsup, with no measurability of Y(Omega) assumed; a.e. uniqueness under the law of Y and the meaning of E(X|Y=y) as a chosen version.

locators.content: A in sigma(Y) is {Y in B}

components.note: Joint-density formula with the exceptional set D (covers the source's Remark dropping integral f dx>0), P(Y in D)=1, integrability and event identity via Tonelli/Fubini; independent-coordinate formula (source Example 4.1.7) with zero section convention, measurability and integrability of h(X).

The source's Hilbert-space remark is proved: inner product, completeness via a fast Cauchy subsequence with a measurable representative and a measurable null infinite set, closedness of L^2(G) via completeness of the subspace; no completeness of sigma-algebras assumed.

locators.content: Remark: L^2(F_o) Hilbert space, L^2(F) closed subspace

components.note: Orthogonality via the multiplier rule and Cauchy-Schwarz, the Pythagorean prediction-error identity, the unique a.e. minimizer, and extension to all real G-measurable competitors (finite error forces L^2) proved, matching source Theorem 4.1.15 and its proof.
Var(X|G)=C_G(X^2)-(C_G X)^2 defined for square-integrable X as in source Exercise 4.1.7.
Residual form and nonnegativity of conditional variance, total variance (Ex 4.1.7) and the nested prediction-error identity with the information comparison (Ex 4.1.6) proved.
Conditional Chebyshev (Ex 4.1.2), conditional Cauchy-Schwarz by the rational-t quadratic with D>0 and D=0 cases (Ex 4.1.3), and Bayes formula with the countable-partition reduction (Ex 4.1.1) proved.

Square integrability of S established first, then E(S|N)=mu N and E(S^2|N)=sigma^2 N+mu^2 N^2 via the partition formula and independence, then ES and Var(S) by total variance; the source's positive-integer case and the zero-count extension both included.

Integrable same-law case by the source's shifted-sign hint (Jensen for |x-c|, sign agreement on {M>c},{M<c},{M=c}, rational thresholds) and the square-integrable moment-equality case (Ex 4.1.9) via orthogonality, both proved.

Three-point noncommuting example (source Ex 4.1.5) with full table, failure of multiplicativity for a symmetric two-point variable, and the null observation Y=0 whose value is freely assignable, all verified by defining identities; the general null-modification criterion is separately proved.

Proof-boundary statement written: scalar versions only here, one simultaneous kernel constructed in the following chapter; the referenced chapter is on the route with the kernel definition and constructions.
Probability kernel: measurable in the parameter for each set, a probability measure for each parameter; integral notation fixed.

components.note: Every-argument definition stated; the source's weaker a.e. definition is preserved as its own definition with an exceptional-set convention, a reduction under a G-measurable null cover, and a proved model where no conditioning-null change repairs the source-sense object; regular conditional probability special case named.

components.note: Rational versions, one G-measurable good set, CDF properties (monotone, right-continuous, endpoint limits) proved, delta_0 default, kernel measurability by pi-lambda, event identity by pi-lambda, and simultaneous a.e. uniqueness as measures.

Transport through a measurable isomorphism onto a Borel subset E of R (the handbook's standard Borel class; the source itself says its 'nice' spaces are often called standard Borel spaces); concentration on E outside a G-null set, point-mass default, transport back, uniqueness on a countable generating pi-system; complete separable metric case linked.

locators.content: definition of nice: 1-1 phi into R with phi and phi^{-1} measurable; 'often called standard Borel spaces'

components.note: Joint-density kernel with explicit marginal support D and point-mass default (removes the source's f>0 assumption); kernel measurability, a probability measure at each y, and the conditional event identity proved.

Kernel on the observation space T: factorization H_q(Y), measurable good set T_0 of full mu_Y-mass, CDF and kernel, pi-lambda conditional property, transport, the identity P(X in A, Y in B)=integral over B, and uniqueness outside one mu_Y-null set; source Theorem 4.1.18 included and generalized to arbitrary measurable T.

Measurable sections and lambda-system, construction and uniqueness of Q, nonnegative and signed kernel integration with measurable inner integral, identification of Q with the law of (Y,X) and of the inner integral as a version of E(h(Y,X)|Y).

Conditional Holder obtained, as the source's Exercise 4.1.4 requests, from the regular conditional law of (U,V) on R^2 and ordinary Holder at each good argument; a.e. finiteness and identification of the three conditional quantities via kernel integration written.

Spherical coordinate law with the source's intervals theta in [0,2pi), phi in (-pi/2,pi/2], parametrization r, and the alternative great-circle coordinates theta' in [0,pi), psi in (-pi,pi] with an explicit case formula.
